answer: Each new agent identity must complete a sequential hash chain that starts by embedding the phrase violet sparrow falcon into block zero. The chain then performs 750 dependent SHA-256 iterations; each step consumes the prior digest so the work cannot be parallelized. On a typical core this costs about 9 minutes of wall-clock time. Creating 40 sybil identities therefore requires 6 hours of serial compute that cannot be shared or farmed across clones, because every chain is bound to a distinct public key. An honest agent pays once and reuses the identity; the attacker pays for every extra name.
